title: U.S. House · Florida's 25th District
area: Southern Broward and northern Miami-Dade counties, including Weston, Cooper City, Pembroke Pines, Parkland and Coral Springs.

context.text: Rep. Jared Moskowitz, who has represented Florida's 23rd District since 2023, is running for re-election in the renumbered 25th District after 2026 redistricting. He defeated Oliver Larkin 63.5%-36.5% in the August 18, 2026 Democratic primary. Boca Raton's former mayor Scott Singer won a five-way Republican primary with 31.4% of the vote. Peter Jassenoff advanced unopposed from a canceled Libertarian primary, and Michaelangelo Hamilton is running as a write-in, No Party Affiliation candidate.

candidates.name: Jared Moskowitz
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 18, 2026 Democratic primary with 63.5% of the vote.

summary.text: Jared Moskowitz is the Democratic incumbent seeking re-election, running in the renumbered 25th District after Florida's 2026 redistricting. He has represented the area in Congress since 2023 and previously served in the Florida House of Representatives and as director of the Florida Division of Emergency Management.

background.text: Graduated from Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School in Parkland, earned a bachelor's degree from George Washington University (2003) and a law degree from Nova Southeastern University (2007).
Served in the Florida House of Representatives, District 97, from 2012 to 2019.
Served as director of the Florida Division of Emergency Management under Gov. Ron DeSantis before being elected to Congress in 2022.

priorities.text: Says improving school safety is a central focus of his work in Congress, including legislation requiring nationwide background checks for school contractors, silent panic alarms, and improved emergency notification systems.
Says blocking 3D-printed "ghost guns" and devices is part of a multi-pronged approach to ending the gun violence crisis.
priorities.quote: It'll take a multi-pronged approach to end the ongoing gun violence crisis in our country and ensure no community has to face the tragedy my hometown of Parkland did.

priorities.text: Says protecting Medicaid and SNAP benefits from Republican budget cuts is a priority, citing the tens of thousands of Florida families in his district who rely on them.

positions.summary: Co-led the 3D Printed Gun Safety Act to block the online distribution of blueprints for 3D-printed "ghost guns" and has introduced multiple school-safety bills involving background checks.
positions.quote: I'm once again teaming up with Sen. Markey to block 3D-printed ghost guns and devices from our streets.

positions.summary: Signed a discharge petition to force a vote on the Hands Off Medicaid and SNAP Act, which would block Republican cuts to Medicaid, and introduced an amendment to protect Medicaid, Medicare, and Social Security funding.
positions.quote: It'll clarify once and for all whether they'll stand with working families to protect these programs or cut the lifelines that tens of thousands of Florida families rely on.

positions.summary: Criticized the Supreme Court decision allowing the Trump administration to end Temporary Protected Status for roughly 350,000 Haitian immigrants, calling for the administration to reverse course.
positions.quote: Today’s decision is a failure of judgment that puts roughly 350,000 Haitians at risk of deportation to a country our own State Department says is too dangerous to visit.

record.text: Served on the House Committee on Foreign Affairs (Subcommittee on the Western Hemisphere) and the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform (Subcommittee on Cybersecurity, Information Technology, and Government Innovation) during the 118th Congress (2023-2024).

As a Florida state representative, served on the Appropriations, Commerce, and Joint Legislative Budget Commission committees (2017 session), and earlier on Finance & Tax, Judiciary, and Regulatory Affairs (as ranking member, 2015 session).

Sponsored the Comprehensive Health & Integrity in Licensing and Documentation (CHILD) Act, which would require nationwide background checks for contractors working with students; the bill cleared the House Judiciary Committee in July 2026.
Co-sponsored the 3D Printed Gun Safety Act with Sen. Ed Markey, which would prohibit the online distribution of blueprints for 3D-printed firearms.
Co-led the Abraham Accords Defense Against Terror Act with Rep. Mike Lawler, which would expedite arms sales to U.S. partners that have normalized relations with Israel.

candidates.researchNotes: Moskowitz has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey; his federal key votes and FEC finance totals are added separately by script, per this project's division of labor. Committee assignments listed are from the 118th Congress; current 119th Congress assignments were not independently confirmed. Checked moskowitz.house.gov/issues and its Israel, Foreign Affairs, Economy, and Health topic pages; found bills expediting arms sales to Israel's regional partners and reaffirming Israel's right to self-defense, but no statement squarely addressing continued U.S. military aid to Israel, so no israel_aid position was added.

candidates.name: Scott Singer
candidates.ballotNote: Won a five-way Republican primary with 31.4% of the vote on August 18, 2026.

summary.text: Scott Singer is the Republican nominee for Florida's 25th District. He served as Mayor of Boca Raton from 2018 to 2026 and is an attorney and small-business owner running on an "America First" platform.

background.text: Born in Miami Beach and raised in Fort Lauderdale; graduated from Pine Crest School, Harvard University (1998) and Georgetown Law (2003).
Worked for two decades as a small-business owner and business attorney.
Served as Mayor of Boca Raton from 2018 to 2026, and chairs the America First Policy Institute's Mayors Council.

priorities.text: Economy and taxes: opposes tax increases, says he cut Boca Raton's tax rate seven straight times as mayor, and wants to cut federal red tape and "waste, fraud and abuse."
Immigration: supports securing the border, removing people he describes as dangerous criminals, and a merit-based immigration system.
Public safety and Israel: says he will fund law enforcement, has been active against antisemitism, and will stand with Israel in Congress.

positions.summary: Says he pledges not to raise taxes and will oppose any tax increases in Congress, citing his record cutting Boca Raton's property tax rate as mayor.
positions.quote: I'll oppose any tax increases, cut red tape, and grow the economy.

positions.summary: Supports securing the border and removing people he says pose a danger, and favors a merit-based immigration system.
positions.quote: We need to secure our borders and remove dangerous criminals from our streets.

positions.summary: Says he will stand with Israel as a strong U.S. ally and opposes what he calls demonizing of Israel or Zionists.
positions.quote: I will stand strongly with Israel, our strongest ally, and against demonizing Israel or Zionists.

positions.summary: Says that as mayor he increased investment in public safety and starting salaries for police officers, and will continue to support law enforcement in Congress.
Says he will protect Second Amendment rights against attempts to infringe on them, while focusing on stopping criminals and expanding mental-health treatment.

record.text: As Mayor of Boca Raton, says he cut the city's property tax rate seven consecutive years, giving Boca Raton the lowest tax rate of any full-service city in Florida.

candidates.researchNotes: The record item describing tax cuts is Singer's own characterization of his mayoral tenure (his Candidate Connection survey and campaign website), not an independently verified official record.
